open.speaker: sarpong
open.text: Good morning. Sit — anywhere. This is UCIS 101, Critical Thinking and Ethics. Every first-year takes it, whether you came here for bridges or for balance sheets.

question.speaker: sarpong
question.text: One question before the syllabus. The night before an exam, someone sends you the questions. You did not ask for them. What do you do? You — yes, you. {name}, is it?

choices.text: Report it to the exams office.
Delete it and tell no one.
Find out who sent it before doing anything.

report.speaker: sarpong
report.text: …That is the right answer. It is not always the easy one — the exams office is a very small room. Write that down, all of you.

delete.speaker: sarpong
delete.text: Tidy. Honest, even. But think about who your silence protects. The person who sent it is grateful for it.

read.speaker: sarpong
read.text: The back row laughs. I don't. "Everybody else will" is how every scandal I have ever seen began.

trace.speaker: sarpong
trace.text: A computer scientist. Follow the file to the hand that sent it. Careful — sometimes the hand is attached to someone with more power than you.

close.speaker: sarpong
close.text: Readings are on the portal. And {name} — if you need help keeping up, Abiba Fuseini runs a study circle. She'll be on the Library steps after this. Tell her I sent you.
